lessonRules.text: Stay inside the unit: use only the words, sentences and patterns this unit of the book teaches (words from earlier units are fine for review). Never invent new words or sentences that are not in the book.
Show the book's own pictures for the unit words, so the child sees the same pictures as in class. Use an emoji only when the book has no picture for a word.
Reading uses the book's own reading texts and sentences, word for word (dialogues, chants, short texts) — not new stories.
Keep everything clear and easy for a young child: one idea at a time, very short instructions, familiar pictures, a few choices, cheerful feedback.

items.title: Unit 15: At the football match: Worksheet

objectives: Say face, foot, football and father.
Hear and say the /f/ sound.
Follow and say 'Point to your ___.' and 'That's your ___.'
materials: The app with the book's pictures

steps.activity: Point game with old words: hand, head, hair.
steps.parentScript: Smile and say: 'Point to your hand.' Point to your own hand. Then say: 'Point to your head.' and 'Point to your hair.' Clap after each one and say 'Yes!'

steps.activity: Show the four new word pictures and practice the /f/ sound.
steps.parentScript: Show each picture. Say slowly: 'face', 'foot', 'football', 'father'. Your child repeats. Then put your top teeth on your lip and blow: 'fff'. Say: 'F, f, face.' Your child repeats. Do the same for football and father.

steps.activity: Say the chant from page 67 together.
steps.parentScript: Read the chant line by line: 'F, f, face. Bill has a lovely face. F, f, football. Bill's watching football. F, f, father. Father's watching football.' Your child repeats each line. Say it again together and clap the beat.

steps.activity: Sing the song from page 68 and do the actions.
steps.parentScript: Touch your child's face and say: 'That's your face.' Touch their foot: 'That's your foot.' Then say: 'Point to your face. Point to your foot.' Your child points. Do the same with hair and head. Sing the whole song together once.

steps.activity: Do the quiz in the app, then trace the word 'face' and 'foot'.
steps.parentScript: Open the quiz and read each question aloud. Let your child choose. Say 'Great job!' for every try. Then write 'face' and 'foot' lightly and let your child trace them. End with a high five.

data.pattern: How many ___ can you see? I can see ___.

questions.prompt: Match the pictures and the words.

objectives: Say the Ww words: window, washing, Wendy, water.
Ask and answer: How many windows can you see? I can see six.
Chant and sing the unit songs.
materials: A cup of water and a sponge

steps.activity: Count from one to ten together, clapping each number.
steps.parentScript: Say: "One, two, three, four!" Clap each number. Keep going to ten. Then say: "Your turn!" and clap while your child counts.

steps.activity: Point to the book pictures and say the Ww words. Make the /w/ sound with round lips.
steps.parentScript: Point to each picture. Say: "W, w, window." Child repeats. Then: "water", "washing", "Wendy". Show round lips for /w/. Show the real water and sponge and say: "Water! Washing!"

steps.activity: Walk around the home and count windows using the pattern.
steps.parentScript: Point to the windows. Ask: "How many windows can you see?" Help your child count, then say: "I can see ___." Child repeats the full answer. Say: "Great counting!"

steps.activity: Do the chant and the song from the book with actions.
steps.parentScript: Say the chant: "W, w, window. How many windows? Six or seven." Draw a window in the air. Then sing: "One, two, three, four. Wendy's at her bedroom door." Knock on a door!

steps.activity: Quick picture check and praise.
steps.parentScript: Point to the book pictures. Ask: "What is it?" Child says window, water, washing, Wendy. Say: "Super job! High five!"

steps.activity: Hello and goodbye game.
steps.parentScript: Wave and say: "Hi, [child's name]!" Help your child say: "Hello, Mom!" Walk to the door, wave and say: "Goodbye!" Child says: "Bye!" Do it two times.

steps.activity: Picture words: show each picture in the app and say the word.
steps.parentScript: Show the teddy bear picture. Say: "Teddy bear." Child repeats. Do the same for foot, face, hands, tiger, turtle, window, football. Then say: "Point to your face." "Point to your foot." Clap for each right answer.

steps.activity: Read the Phil and Sue story together.
steps.parentScript: Open page 72. Read one line, point to the words, and the child repeats. At the end, hold up the teddy bear and say: "Look! I can see a teddy bear." Child repeats. Then say: "It's Lucy's teddy bear!"

steps.activity: "I can see" spy game and first sounds.
steps.parentScript: Point to a window and say: "Look!" Help the child say: "I can see a window." Then say: "Tiger. T, t, tiger!" "Window. W, w, window!" "Football. F, f, football!" Child repeats each one.

steps.activity: Do the quiz in the app.
